newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK money rates ease slightly on HKMA injection.
newsitem.headline: HK money rates ease slightly on HKMA injection.

text.p: Hong Kong interbank rates were slightly easier in quiet trading on Monday following an injection by the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA), dealers said.
The HKMA, the de facto central bank, said earlier it injected HK$598 million into the market in view of the tight liquidity in the local cash market.
"Rates fell slightly in reaction to the injection, otherwise the market was quiet," a dealer said.
Overnight cash eased to 5-1/8 1/16 from 5-5/16 3/8 on Friday and three-month was at 5-17/32 15/32 against 5-9/16 1/2 percent.
Interbank rates were seen trapped in tight ranges although the market should remain tight ahead of the month-end and the start of the HKMA's Real Time Gross Settlement on December 9, dealers said.
The HKMA would continue to monitor market movements and would step in if action was needed, a U.S. bank dealer said.
Trading in government paper was moderate with even demand across the board, dealers said.
"Government paper yield moved narrowly since U.S. treasuries closed flat on Friday," one said.
One-week note yield was 4.97 versus 5.00 percent, three-year notes yielded 6.06 percent versus 6.08 on Thursday.
The seven-year and 10-year notes were unchanged, yielding 6.89 and 7.15 percent, respectively.
